notes: v2 merges the former separate `seo_pillar_page` asset into this single stage. Master_Prompt_Universal_Page_Design_v1.md is now v2.0 of that prompt: it carries the SEO/competitor-benchmark pass (Step 2, Rules 8-9, PART 2 and PART 4) that used to justify a second run of the same file, so there is no longer a design-only pass followed by an SEO variant pass — one stage designs the page from the reference's visual system AND benchmarks its architecture against the competitor pillar pages surfaced by `competitor_analysis_seo_pillar_page` (assets/Prompts/Competitor Analysis/05_SEO_Pillar_Page.md), which is now this stage's paired competitor prepass. `seo_pillar_page.json` was removed in the same change; see DAG_SOURCE_MAP.md row 3.

fields.label: Client Name
fields.raw_explanation: YOUR ANSWER

fields.label: Client Website URL
fields.raw_explanation: YOUR ANSWER

fields.label: Reference Design Source
fields.raw_explanation: UPLOAD / URL / SCREENSHOT of the page whose visual design to replicate

fields.label: Reference Design Scope
choices: A DIFFERENT PAGE ON THE SAME SITE
fields.raw_explanation: FULL SITE STYLE / THIS ONE PAGE ONLY / A DIFFERENT PAGE ON THE SAME SITE

fields.label: Services / Sub-Services to Cover
fields.raw_explanation: LIST — one per line, with the URL of each service's existing page where it has one / NONE. Picked from the services (Phase 1) or sub-services (Phase 2) linked from the reference page (or the main landing page when there is no reference page), plus any the operator types. One combined pillar page covers every listed service. Each selected service's own page is read automatically at generation time and appended as SOURCE CONTENT; blank means the page covers what the Improved Page Content covers.

fields.label: Improved Page Content
fields.raw_explanation: UPLOAD OR PASTE — the full rewritten page copy. Normally the CRO stage's (Master_Prompt_Universal_Page_Rewrite_v1.md) Part 2 output, but this prompt also runs standalone on any finished copy if pasted directly. If it includes a CRO audit or mode-resolution table, ignore that — design the final page copy only.

fields.label: Locked Sections (from CRO)
fields.raw_explanation: Synthesized field — per the cross-cutting DAG rule, any section CRO marked as locked stays locked through every later stage that touches page copy, including Pillar Page.

fields.label: Page Architecture / Section Order
fields.raw_explanation: LIST ALL SECTIONS IN ORDER, or write "USE CONTENT ORDER" to follow the content file's own structure, or "USE DEFAULT" for the 13-section universal architecture

fields.label: New Sections to Add (optional)
fields.raw_explanation: LIST / NONE

fields.label: Primary Keyword / Head Term
fields.raw_explanation: YOUR ANSWER — the single term this pillar page must own. Added in v2 with the merged SEO pass: Step 0 item 8 resolves the search-structure requirements from it (single H1 carrying its intent, an H2 per sub-topic, jump navigation, cluster links), and it is also what the paired competitor prepass uses as its {SERVICE} placeholder when searching for competitor pillar pages on this topic.

fields.label: Secondary / Cluster Terms (optional)
fields.raw_explanation: LIST / NONE

fields.label: Internal Cluster Pages to Link (optional)
fields.raw_explanation: LIST URLs + what each covers / NONE. Rule 9 places each of these in the section that page belongs to, with descriptive anchor text — a genuine pillar page links out to its cluster.

fields.label: Competitor Analysis — Pillar Pages
fields.raw_explanation: PASTE OR ATTACH — the competitor pillar-page listing produced by the paired `competitor_analysis_seo_pillar_page` stage (05_SEO_Pillar_Page.md). Not an invisible prepass: because the search has to be run on THIS page's topic (`primary_keyword_head_term`, an intake answer), the UI asks the operator mid-intake whether to research it or to supply their own list, then shows the found competitors for approval before they reach this field. Step 2 extracts architecture, depth and coverage patterns from it and decides ADOPT / EXCEED / SKIP per pattern; competitor copy, claims and branding are explicitly out of bounds. Left unavailable, Step 0 item 7 degrades the run to design-only rather than inventing competitors.

fields.label: Word for the reader
fields.raw_explanation: e.g. patient / client / customer / homeowner / operator. Per REVIEW_NEEDED_V2.md item 4 resolution, auto-pulled from the CRO stage's cro_terminology_map write-key ("match the copy prompt's resolution — keeps design and content consistent") instead of being re-entered.

fields.label: Word for the thing being chosen between
